text: 🇲🇽🌎 "You can only have one master, and it is the people of Mexico." — President Claudia Sheinbaum Economic integration with the U.S. "has to be with sovereignty," she said, then walked through the history: Spain refusing to recognize independence until 1836, Texas, the French Pastry War, the U.S. invasion that took more than half the territory, the French invasion, and the 1914 U.S. occupation of Veracruz.

🇲🇽⚖️ "You can't have two flags, you can't have two oaths — you have to have only one." — President Claudia Sheinbaum On the reform barring dual nationals from the presidency and governorships: ambassadors already can't hold dual nationality. Mexicans born in the U.S. are Mexican, she said — but to become president or governor, they would have to renounce U.S. citizenship. "Who do you represent? Your people, or two peoples?"

🇲🇽💧 "There is no other option in Baja California but desalination." — President Claudia Sheinbaum The Rosarito plant — set to be Latin America's largest, 2,200 liters per second in its first stage — begins construction this week to supply Tijuana and Rosarito, over 2 million people. The project was redesigned after an extensive environmental study to mitigate the brine discharged into the Pacific.

🔥🇲🇽 "Former presidents no longer have a pension, since President López Obrador." — President Claudia Sheinbaum Asked about the Bank of Mexico's lifetime pensions — over 130,000 pesos a month for Ernesto Zedillo and 330,000 for Guillermo Ortiz, president and finance secretary during the Fobaproa bank bailout — she said Banxico officials won court injunctions to escape the presidential salary cap, and that "we would have to see whether we continue with those pensions or not." She will seek to make the amounts public.
banner: "FORMER PRESIDENTS NO LONGER HAVE A PENSION"

text: 🔥🇲🇽 $65 million diverted from the Federal Police under Peña Nieto — now 15- and 20-year bans for the officials involved. "The money did go out, but the contract was not paid." — Raquel Buenrostro, Anti-Corruption and Good Government Secretary In 2015 the Federal Police signed a $130 million intelligence-services contract; $65 million was then withdrawn as "national security expenses" and never reached it. The former intelligence chief and former secretary general of the Federal Police are barred from public office, repayment of the $65 million is being sought, and a criminal case is open with the Attorney General.

🔥🇲🇽 Mexico's anti-corruption ministry prevented nearly 84 billion pesos in irregular spending in two years. "We consider that preventing is a better result for all the people, for all Mexicans." — Raquel Buenrostro, Anti-Corruption and Good Government Secretary Breakdown: 42 billion pesos in avoided public-works overcharges, 29 billion from better procurement, 7.8 billion from restructuring government, 4.8 billion in fines collected. 4,193 officials sanctioned; 517 criminal complaints filed with the Attorney General.

‍LATIN TIMES: Sheinbaum's Second Grito Draws Mexico's Biggest Zócalo Crowd Yet September 16, 2026 | 🟢 📰 Credit where due: Latin Times reports 300,000+ packed the Zócalo — topping her 2025 record — for Sheinbaum's Independence address and its message to Washington. 🇲🇽 "Aquí somos mexicanos y nadie vendrá a decirnos qué hacer" — here we are Mexicans, and no one will tell us what to do. • "no vamos a firmar nada que tenga que ver con una afectación" (we won't sign anything that harms us) • 300,000+ in the Zócalo, topping 2025

‍AMERICAS QUARTERLY: Mexico's Homicides Are Falling, but a Broader Violence Crisis Persists September 17, 2026 | 🟡 📰 AS/COA's outlet concedes what most US media buries: the "daily average of intentional homicides has fallen 51%," and Sheinbaum "significantly improved" the state's capacity against organized crime. Then comes the "but." 🇲🇽 The headline does the work — credit in the subordinate clause, doubt in the main one. • "the daily average of intentional homicides has fallen 51%" • Sheinbaum "significantly improved... capacity to fight organized crime"

‍CNN: Mexico acted urgently for a Spanish victim — "not enough" for its own September 21, 2026 | 🟡 📰 CNN uses the murder of Spanish student Claudia Tacoronte to frame Mexico as neglecting its own femicide victims, sourcing the charge to a University of San Diego professor. 🔍 The data is real — Morelos logged 21 femicides Jan–July — but the "urgency only for foreigners" angle is the outlet's editorial choice. • "not doing enough for female victims at home" • "cases don't result in the identification of a suspect"
